request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient: 44-year-old male
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:

The patient presented at our primary care clinic with a lump in the right nipple associated with sharp pain. The mammogram revealed a 1.2 cm mass in the right retro areolar breast. Core needle biopsy was positive for invasive ductal carcinoma ER+ and PR+ and negative for HER2-. The patient underwent simple mastectomy and right sentinel lymph node biopsy. He received dose-dense adjuvant chemotherapy which was stopped after 3 doses of Taxanes. The lymph node biopsy came back positive for metastatic carcinoma, and the patient received radiation therapy. The patient was started on Tamoxifen therapy for>5 years.

Summary:

The 44-year-old male was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma stage IIA. He underwent simple mastectomy, right sentinel lymph node biopsy, radiation therapy, and chemotherapy. He was started on Tamoxifen therapy for>5 years. He denied any active complaints 3 years post diagnosis. The physical examination was positive for old healed lateral scar on the right chest. Genetic testing revealed no evidence of BRCA mutations or other evidence of familial breast cancer. The patient's annual mammographic screening and clinical exam of the contralateral breast were normal. He reported concerns of trouble maintaining erections and weight gain which were likely secondary to the effect of Tamoxifen.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The episode described is a male patient with invasive ductal carcinoma of the right retroareolar breast, which is a malignant neoplasm of the breast. In ICD-10-AM, C50 covers malignant neoplasm of the breast and includes male breast cancer.

The summary also mentions metastatic carcinoma in the lymph node. This is a secondary neoplasm and would be coded separately as C77. The primary site is the principal diagnosis.

Some of the content describes a later follow-up, with Tamoxifen side effects and surveillance. Even so, the condition chiefly responsible for the episode is still the breast carcinoma. If the episode were purely a follow-up after completed treatment, a Z-code such as Z08 or Z85 would apply. However, the course described covers the diagnosis, mastectomy, chemotherapy and radiation, and the patient is still on active hormonal therapy. The malignancy is therefore treated as the principal diagnosis.

CODE: C50
